c.tagline: Windswept Atlantic medina of blue boats, ramparts, and Gnaoua rhythm.

taxi.fareNote: Small blue 'petits taxis' handle trips inside town — metered by law but many run short flat fares (around 10-20 DH); larger cream 'grands taxis' cover the airport and out-of-town runs. No Uber or Bolt operate in Essaouira.

emergency.note: 19 reaches the police in towns and cities; 15 is the ambulance/medical emergency line (177 for the Gendarmerie Royale on rural roads).

hood_landmark.Diabat: Diabat Essaouira Borj el Berod ruins
hood_landmark.Kasbah: Skala de la Ville Essaouira clock tower

avoid.reason: Politely brush off faux guides and touts around the medina and port, watch pockets in crowded souks, and skip unlit medina alleys late at night.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed walled old town, a compact grid of whitewashed, blue-shuttered lanes packed with souks, artisan workshops, riads, and the fish-grilling port at its edge; the obvious first-timer base, everything on foot.
The oldest fortified quarter of the medina by the Skala ramparts and the clock tower, lined with galleries, cafes, and the town's grandest riads; central and atmospheric.

A quieter, more residential pocket of the eastern medina near Bab Doukkala, with local bakeries, small guesthouses, and everyday markets rather than tourist souks; a calmer, authentic base still inside the walls.

The newer district stretching south along the Atlantic beachfront below the medina, home to seafront hotels, surf and kitesurf schools, and wide open sand; best for water-sports travelers wanting room and sea breeze.

A small village across the Oued Ksob about 10 minutes south, backed by dunes and the ruined Borj el Berod fort, with the Sofitel golf resort and a laid-back rural feel; suits those wanting quiet, riding, and golf away from the crowds.
lodging: Le Médina Essaouira Thalassa Sea & Spa - MGallery

water.note: Tap is treated but most visitors drink bottled water.

transit.hours: Petits taxis run through the day and evening; the medina is walkable at all hours.
transit.note: Essaouira is small and almost entirely walkable within the walled medina; there is no urban bus network, so short hops rely on blue petits taxis.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (dirhams); confirm the fare or that the meter is running before setting off.

bus: CTM & Supratours coaches to Marrakech, Agadir & Casablanca
Local grands taxis to nearby towns
train: No rail service — nearest station is Marrakech (~3 hr by coach)

transit.m: Grand taxi (shared/cream) to the medina (~15 min)

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; round up for cafes and taxis. A few dirhams for porters and parking wardens is the norm.
